title: 3 Signals That Separate a Liquidity Flush from a Bear Market

beats.text: Every crash starts the same way: red screens, falling gold, and panic headlines. Watching price alone won't tell you whether it's a forced flush or a real bear market. Institutions watch three deeper signals instead.

Signal one: corporate junk credit. In true systemic bear markets, high-yield bonds crack first as defaults loom. Yet right now, while Bitcoin dropped twenty-three percent and gold fell thirteen, high-yield credit barely moved — down under two percent from its November high.
Credit isn't panicking. That tells you leverage is liquidating — not the real economy collapsing.

Signal two: the VIX term structure. Normally, three-month volatility costs more than thirty-day panic. Today, spot VIX spiked near thirty — pushing the VIX-to-three-month ratio to one point one zero. Extreme inversion signals emergency hedging near peak liquidation.

Signal three is the missing green light: the Dollar and gold turn. Ten-year Treasury yields eased slightly off their five point one five percent peak, but the U.S. Dollar remains pinned near one hundred and four, keeping pressure on gold and risk assets.

Put all three together. Credit is green, volatility inversion is amber, and the Dollar is still red. Until the Dollar rolls over and gold decouples higher, volatility stays violent — but without a credit crack, this still looks like a flush, not a structural bear market.
Watch credit, volatility inversion, and the Dollar — not the headlines. In Episode Two, we trace how margin calls cascade across portfolios in real time. Subscribe to How Markets Break.
